bib.title: Mercury: Ultra-Fast Language Models Based on Diffusion

question: Can a diffusion-based LLM be scaled to commercial size and give much higher token throughput than autoregressive models at comparable code quality?
hypothesis: Parallel coarse-to-fine token generation uses GPUs better than autoregressive decoding, giving a better speed-quality frontier.
contributions: Describes the Mercury family of diffusion LLMs (dLLMs).
Up to 10x faster than frontier speed-optimized LLMs, over 1000 tokens/sec on H100s.
Coding models comparable in quality to high-speed commercial offerings on coding benchmarks.

method.summary: Transformer-based diffusion LLMs (Mercury Coder Mini and Small) trained with a denoising diffusion loss, generating multiple tokens in parallel in a coarse-to-fine way, served on a proprietary dynamically batched inference engine with custom kernels. Evaluated by Artificial Analysis for speed and on code benchmarks and Copilot Arena.
method.task: code generation / fill-in-the-middle with diffusion language models

datasets.name: Proprietary pretraining mix (web crawls plus curated real and synthetic data)
MultiPL-E
datasets.split: C++, Java, JS, PHP, Bash, TS

models.name: Autoregressive baselines (Llama 3.1 8B, Qwen 2.5 Coder, Mistral Small 3, DeepSeek Coder V2 Lite, Nova Micro, Codestral 2501, GPT 4o Mini, Claude 3.5 Haiku, Gemini 2.0 Flash Lite, DeepSeek V3, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, GPT 4o)

training.objective: L(x) = -E_t[gamma(t) E_{z_t~q} log p_theta(x|z_t)], denoising diffusion loss with noise-level weight gamma(t)>=0

other.fine_tuning: RLHF or DPO possible by swapping the autoregressive loss for the diffusion loss; not reported as done

inference.decoding: iterative parallel denoising from noise, coarse-to-fine; number of diffusion steps not stated
inference.prompting: zero-shot, few-shot and chain-of-thought supported; prompts used in evals not given

other.engine: proprietary inference engine, dynamically batched sampling and paging, custom kernels; OpenAI-compatible API

metrics.name: pass@1

metrics.name: throughput
metrics.definition: output tokens divided by processing time from first token to last, median over cloud providers (Artificial Analysis)

metrics.name: Elo / latency

limits: Proprietary: parameters, architecture sizes, data, optimizer, steps, diffusion step count and inference engine are not disclosed.
Speed measured by a third party on proprietary prompts; quality benchmarks lack seeds or variance.
Only coding models; Mini is below several baselines on LiveCodeBench (17.0 vs Claude 3.5 Haiku 31.0).
Scaling claim rests on only two sizes (Small better than Mini).

terms.definition: diffusion large language model, generating tokens in parallel in a coarse-to-fine way

lineage.work: Discrete diffusion language modeling by estimating the ratios of the data distribution (Lou, Meng, Ermon)
lineage.note: Mercury methods extend [28] with data and compute changes to scale

lineage.work: Efficient training of language models to fill in the middle
